Energy transition

Load Shedding

Coal plants in your Johannesburg utility are breaking down faster than they can be repaired. Diesel can keep the lights on, if you can pay the fuel bill.

Play Load Shedding↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
Johannesburg, South Africa
Starts in
2016
Your term
7 years

Your starting point

You take over in 2016 with a scaled version of South Africa's fleet. Alongside coal, you have a little nuclear, diesel, wind and solar generation.

Breakdowns leave you with less coal power each year. Diesel can cover some of the shortfall while you build, but every delay means buying more fuel.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Plan around the plants that still work

    Check how much coal power is actually available before deciding how much new capacity to order.

  2. 02

    Budget for diesel

    Work out how long you'll need emergency generation before a replacement opens. Can the utility afford to run it for that long?

  3. 03

    Check the replacement after dark

    Look for hours when the new fleet still falls short. If those gaps remain, you'll still need the diesel plant.

How soon can you give the diesel generators a break?
